formal_cot_trace.natural_language: A nitroso group is characterized by a nitrogen atom double-bonded to an oxygen atom (-N=O). The standard SMARTS pattern for this motif is `[N]=[O]`. In a nitro group (`-NO2`, represented in SMILES as `[N+](=O)[O-]`), the nitrogen is bonded to two oxygen atoms. Because these two N-O bonds are equivalent due to resonance, many cheminformatics systems either represent the nitro group in a hypervalent state (`N(=O)=O`) or use resonance-aware matching, which results in both N-O bonds being matched as `N=O` motifs. To capture both bonds in standard RDKit representations, the generalized SMARTS `[N]~[O]` can be used as an equivalent.
